findings.explanation: The cleanup_policies block (id "DELETE-TAGGED") has action = "DELETE" and a condition that only checks tag_state = "TAGGED", with no older_than/newer_than bound. Artifact Registry cleanup runs periodically and will match and delete every tagged image the moment this policy is active — including images currently deployed — since there's no age or version-count restriction narrowing the match. holden's existing HLD_GCP_341 only checks that a cleanup_policies block exists, so it doesn't catch this: the block is present, but its DELETE condition is unbounded. Because this file lives under example/, it's also the reference pattern anyone copies when wiring up a real repository.
findings.remediation: Add an older_than (or newer_than) bound to the DELETE condition so only stale tagged images are removed, e.g. older_than = "2592000s" (30 days). If the intent really is to delete every tagged image unconditionally, that's unusual enough to warrant a comment explaining why.
findings.title: Cleanup policy deletes all tagged artifacts with no age/version bound

suggested_policies.rationale: holden's HLD_GCP_341 only verifies a cleanup_policies block exists on google_artifact_registry_repository; it doesn't check that a DELETE action is scoped by age or version count. A DELETE policy with only a tag_state condition matches every artifact in that state unconditionally, which is a real production footgun (this repo's own example/ ships exactly that pattern) and is unambiguous to detect structurally.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_514
name: Artifact Registry DELETE cleanup policies must be scoped by age or version count
cloud: gcp
principle: reliability
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A cleanup_policies entry with action DELETE and only a tag_state/tag_prefixes
  condition (no older_than/newer_than) matches every artifact in that state
  immediately, deleting actively-deployed images the moment the cleanup job
  next runs. This can break rollbacks and redeploys with no warning.
message: |
  cleanup_policies action DELETE has no older_than/newer_than condition, so it
  deletes every matching artifact regardless of age.
remediation: |
  Add an age-based bound to the DELETE condition, e.g.:

    cleanup_policies {
      id     = "delete-old-tagged"
      action = "DELETE"
      condition {
        tag_state  = "TAGGED"
        older_than = "2592000s" # 30 days
      }
    }
resources:
  google_artifact_registry_repository:
    path: cleanup_policies
    not_any:
      all:
        - path: action
          equals: DELETE
        - path: condition.older_than
          absent: true
        - path: condition.newer_than
          absent: true
